name: Falmouth
title: Falmouth Thickness Gauging: Ship Repair and Bunker Calls
description: Ultrasonic thickness measurement in Falmouth at the docks, bunkering anchorage and lay-up moorings: pre-docking gauging, renewal survey, hull structure.
h1: Thickness Measurement for Ships at Falmouth Docks and Anchorages
intro: Falmouth's deep natural harbour at the western end of the English Channel has long been a place for ships to stop: for bunkers and stores at the anchorage, for repairs in the docks, and for lay-up in the Carrick Roads. Each of these keeps a ship in one place for a while, which is what thickness gauging needs. Atlantis mobilises technicians from India to gauge alongside in the docks, at anchor by launch, or on a laid-up ship on the river moorings.
keywords: thickness measurement for ships at falmouth

highlights.p: Ships stopping in Falmouth Bay for bunkers, stores or crew changes are at anchor for hours to a day. A focused deck, air-pipe and tank scope, prepared in advance by the crew, fits that window.
Falmouth Docks gives the full drydock window for renewal surveys and steel renewal, and the team works to the agreed TM plan alongside the yard's planners and the attending class surveyor.
Ships laid up on the River Fal moorings can be gauged over days rather than hours, giving owners a full condition baseline before reactivation, sale or a return to trading.

port.h: Falmouth: anchorage, repair harbour and lay-up waters
p: Falmouth sits at the entrance to the Carrick Roads, a deep natural harbour formed by the drowned valley of the River Fal, close to the western end of the English Channel. Ships bound up-Channel from the Atlantic, or heading out into it, stop in Falmouth Bay to take bunkers, stores and spare parts, change crew or wait for orders, and the bay's anchorages and bunker supply make it a routine call for tankers, bulk carriers and cargo ships that would otherwise not touch a UK port at all. In westerly gales the bay also gives shelter to ships waiting for better weather before heading out past Land's End.

Falmouth Docks, the ship-repair yard inside the harbour, has drydocks and repair quays and has handled ferries, cruise ships, research vessels, government ships and tankers for many years. The harbour also has a strong superyacht build and refit presence. Further up the Fal, sheltered deep-water moorings have been used over the decades to lay up merchant ships when freight markets are weak, and owners choose them because the river gives shelter that an open roadstead cannot. The docks lie only a short distance from the bay anchorages, so a ship can move from anchor to yard with little transit time.

Inspection demand here follows those uses. At the anchorage, the window is a bunker call of a few hours to a day, which suits targeted gauging of deck, air pipes and accessible tanks, and pre-purchase or on-hire condition checks arranged at short notice by brokers who know the ship will stop. In the docks, renewal surveys and steel renewal call for full TM programmes worked alongside the yard. Laid-up ships offer the longest windows of all, and owners reactivating a ship after lay-up need to know what corrosion has developed while she has been idle, because stagnant ballast and sea-water systems do not stand still metallurgically just because the ship does.

facilities.h: Where gauging is done in and around Falmouth
p: Hull gauging at anchor in Falmouth Bay is launch work. The ship's agent books the launch, the team boards by pilot or accommodation ladder in the lee of the ship, and work stops if the weather turns. The bay is sheltered from the west but more open to easterly and south-easterly winds, so the agent's local knowledge matters when choosing the day, and the scope is ordered so that the most important readings are taken first. Gauges, couplant and probes go up the ladder in a bag, so the kit is chosen for the scope before the launch leaves.

In the docks, a ship on a repair contract has the yard's services, staging and lighting, and the team works to the yard's programme beside the class surveyor. For laid-up ships on the river moorings, access is again by launch, but tanks can be emptied and ventilated over days rather than hours, so a complete condition survey ahead of reactivation or sale is realistic. Ship repair in Falmouth and gauging are closely linked: readings taken at anchor on one call often become the steel list for a docking here on the next.
list: Falmouth Bay anchorage — targeted deck, air-pipe and tank gauging on ships calling for bunkers or stores, reached by launch through the ship's agent.
Falmouth Docks drydocks — double bottoms, shell and tanks gauged while the ship is dry, so the class surveyor and yard can agree renewal before the dock is flooded.
Falmouth Docks repair quays — afloat repair periods for piping, deck and tank work, where gauging confirms which pipe runs and plates need renewal.
Carrick Roads and River Fal moorings — condition surveys on laid-up ships before reactivation, sale or a return to service, with time to open tanks in sequence.
Ships waiting for orders in the bay — pre-purchase and on-hire condition gauging arranged at short notice with the brokers and the agent.

context.h: Sulphur boundaries, port state control and the Western Approaches
p: Falmouth lies on the western edge of the North Sea and English Channel SOx Emission Control Area, whose Channel boundary runs along longitude 5°W close to the harbour entrance, so fuel changeover is part of the routine for ships passing here. Once a ship has been at berth in the harbour for two hours, the UK's at-berth rule requires 0.10% sulphur fuel whatever the ECA boundary says. From 1 September 2028 the North-East Atlantic ECA, adopted by the IMO in 2026, extends the 0.10% limit to the waters west of the UK as well, which closes the gap at the Channel's western end and changes the fuel and scrubber decisions owners make about this route.

Port state control at Falmouth is carried out by the Maritime and Coastguard Agency; the UK kept its place in the Paris MoU after Brexit while applying PSC through domestic law. The ships stopping here are mostly deep-sea tankers, bulk carriers and cargo ships under a wide range of flags and managers, which is why so much of the gauging is commissioned by superintendents in Greece, Germany, Singapore or elsewhere who need a reliable set of readings from a ship they cannot visit themselves. For them, a bunker stop is an opportunity rather than an interruption, and a ship already planning a Falmouth Docks visit can be gauged before she arrives.

jobs.h: Typical thickness gauging jobs in Falmouth
jobs.p: The jobs that come to Falmouth reflect why ships stop here. Most are short and targeted at the anchorage, some are full scopes in the docks, and a few are long condition surveys on idle ships. We plan each one with the ship's agent and the superintendent, and adjust the scope to the weather and to how long the ship will actually be in port.
list: Targeted gauging on a bulk carrier during a bunker call in Falmouth Bay: deck plating, hatch coamings, air pipes and one or two ballast tanks prepared by the crew in advance.
Pre-purchase condition gauging of a product tanker stopping for orders, scoped by the buyer's adviser and done by launch within the ship's stay at anchor.
Renewal-survey gauging on a ferry in drydock at Falmouth Docks, worked alongside the yard and class, with substantial-corrosion areas marked for steel renewal.
Reactivation survey of a ship laid up on the River Fal: shell, tank and piping gauging to find corrosion that developed while the ship was idle.
Piping UT on a research or government vessel during an afloat repair period at the docks, confirming which sea-water and fire-main sections need renewal.

logistics: The team usually flies into Heathrow or Gatwick and continues by rail or road to Cornwall; Cornwall Airport Newquay and Exeter Airport are closer alternatives with domestic and some European connections. Falmouth Docks has controlled gates for which the yard issues passes, while anchorage and river work depends on launches booked by the ship's agent with the harbour's local launch operators. Teams travel from India on UK visas, and because bunker calls can be fixed at short notice, owners who expect to use Falmouth regularly benefit from having the team's visas in place before a specific job arises.

faqs.q: Can you gauge a ship at anchor in Falmouth Bay during a bunker call?
faqs.a: Yes, by launch, within the time the ship is stopped and when the weather allows safe boarding. A bunker call suits a focused scope: deck plating, hatch coamings, air and vent pipes and tanks the crew have prepared in advance. We agree priorities with the superintendent before the call, so the most important readings are taken first in case the ship sails early or the weather closes in.

faqs.q: Do you work on ships in the Falmouth Docks yard?
faqs.a: We do, for the owner or manager of a ship in dock or at the repair quays, not as a yard subcontractor. Gas-freeing, staging and lighting are coordinated through the superintendent and the yard, the agreed TM plan is followed with the class surveyor in attendance, and areas showing substantial or excessive corrosion are marked on the steel so the yard can plan the renewal straight away.

faqs.q: What should a laid-up ship inspection check before reactivation?
faqs.a: It should look at what idleness does to steel: ballast tanks left part-full, sea chests and sea-water piping that stood stagnant, and deck and hatch structure exposed to weather without routine maintenance. Thickness gauging gives a baseline before the ship returns to trading, and helps the owner decide which repairs to do at Falmouth Docks and which can wait for the next drydock.

faqs.q: How is ship inspection in Cornwall arranged with an India-mobilised team?
faqs.a: We ask for the expected call date as early as possible, apply for UK visas, and fix flights to London and onward travel to Falmouth once the ship's agent confirms the stop. For owners with regular Falmouth calls, keeping the visas valid means the team can be sent at shorter notice when a stop is confirmed. Launches and gate passes are arranged through the agent and the yard.
